facts.text: Durant was founded in the early 1870s when the Missouri–Kansas–Texas Railroad reached the area, named after Choctaw pioneer Dixon Durant.
The city sits in the Texoma region, just a short drive from Lake Texoma, giving it a unique southeastern Oklahoma identity.
Fort Washita Historic Site & Museum in Durant offers a glimpse into Oklahoma’s diverse history, including its role in the Indian Territory.
Reba McEntire, the Grammy‑winning country star, grew up in Durant and once performed locally before her national fame.
Dennis Rodman, the Hall‑of‑Fame basketball legend, also attended Southeast Oklahoma State University in Durant during his college years.
Durant’s educational roots trace back to 1901 when Durant Presbyterian College opened, later becoming the present‑day Southeast Oklahoma State University.
